messages:
sarah-support: Hey team, opening this thread on behalf of Jordan (customer) — they're seeing a spike in 429s and quota errors yesterday during a marketing burst. Can someone triage?

jordan-customer: pasting snippet of failures — we saw ~12% 429s for ~4 minutes, then traffic dropped. We were running burst imports to /v1/generate with model `openlm-13b-quant`. Request ID examples: req_01F9X3, req_01F9X4.

alex-runtime: thanks, Jordan. Can you share whether you use the hosted API key or a dedicated instance? Also curious if requests include `max_tokens` spikes.

jordan-customer: hosted API, key pj_abc123, same model across requests, typical max_tokens=512. Traffic pattern was 100 req/s for ~3m, then short pause, then another spike.

marco-ops: quick hypothesis: burst hit global rate limit/quota, not backend instability. On hosted we enforce both per-key token bucket and per-customer daily quota. When the short-term burst depletes the bucket, we return 429 + `x-rw-retry-after`. Can you confirm the exact response headers?

jordan-customer: here are headers from a sample 429 response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, `x-rw-rate-limit: 60/min`, `x-rw-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-reset: 2025-11-14T16:42:10Z`, `x-request-id: req_01F9X3`.

ingrid-telemetry: good, the presence of `x-rw-remaining: 0` points to quota exhaustion for that window. What we need to attribute: was this per-route throttling or per-customer/global? I can check Grafana + logs.

alex-runtime: For triage steps: 1) check request-level logs for those request IDs, 2) correlate with metrics: `api.requests.count` (by route), `api.responses.429` (by api_key/customer/model), and token consumption meter `api.tokens.consumed`. 3) See burst token-bucket headroom: `quota.buckets.{api_key}.tokens`.

ingrid-telemetry: I pulled logs for req_01F9X3 and req_01F9X4 — traces show the rate-limit decision happened at the ingress layer (rate-limiter service) before routing to runtime. So attribution is to API key burst consumption. Query I used in logs: `service:ingress AND request_id:req_01F9X3 | json | fields tenant_id, api_key_id, route, model, token_count`

marco-ops: thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) was the customer's daily quota near zero? 2) did they hit per-minute bucket or per-second burst window? Our config: token bucket refill at 60 tokens/sec, burst capacity 300 tokens.

jordan-customer: daily quota was 100M tokens, only 12M used so far. So it's a short-window burst problem, not daily quota.

alex-runtime: action: add a dashboard panel showing `rate_limit.exhaustions` split by `tenant_id` and `route`. Suggested alert: trigger if 429 ratio > 5% of requests for a tenant over 10m AND absolute requests > 50/min. That helps avoid noisy alerts for low-traffic tenants.

ingrid-telemetry: I created a Grafana panel draft and a log alert. Panel queries: PromQL sample: `sum by(tenant_id,route) (increase(api_responses_total{code="429"}[10m])) / sum by(tenant_id,route) (increase(api_requests_total[10m]))` and `sum by(tenant_id) (increase(api_tokens_consumed_total[10m]))`.

marco-ops: also add a panel for `quota.bucket_tokens{api_key}` to visualize headroom. For attribution to model, include label `model_id` on rate_limit metrics so we can see if a particular model variant causes more token pressure.

jordan-customer: is there any recommended client-side behavior? We have a few workers that back off poorly and retry aggressively.

alex-runtime: yes — implement exponential backoff with jitter and respect `x-rw-retry-after` header when present. Also, for bulk imports, use the batch endpoints or contact us for a temporary burst raise (we can increase per-minute capacity for short windows or suggest using Dedicated).

ingrid-telemetry: note for dashboards/alerts: include the `model_id` and `route` tags on each metric emitted by runtime and ingress. If you don't have those tags, attribution is much harder. We're adding an enforcement to always attach `model_id` at ingress.

marco-ops: recorded runbook steps to support docs channel: how to triage 429s and 503s -> summarizing: 1) confirm response headers, 2) fetch logs for request IDs, 3) check Grafana 10m/1h panels for 429 ratio and token consumption, 4) check quota service for bucket state, 5) check for retries causing amplified traffic.

sarah-support: Jordan — can I ping you to coordinate a short replay window so we can see live metrics while you reproduce? Also asking infra to temporarily lift per-minute soft limits if required.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: rate-limiter config change rolled back at 2025-11-14T17:05:00Z (not related to Jordan's incident window).

alex-runtime: one more debugging snippet for engineers — to quickly repro and collect headers/logs run:```bash
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H \"Authorization: Bearer pj_abc123\" \\
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
    -d '{\"model\":\"openlm-13b-quant\",\"input\":\"test\",\"max_tokens\":512}' \\
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.01
done
```This simulates burst ~100-200 req/s and will show 429s if you exhaust the bucket. Collect `x-rw-*` headers from responses.

ingrid-telemetry: follow-on: I've added tags and a temporary alert in prod Grafana: `Alert: Tenant 429 ratio > 5% (10m)` -> notify #support and #eng-runtime with tenant, top routes, and top models. Also adding a playbook link.

jordan-customer: thanks — we'll run the repro in a staging key and then coordinate a short live test. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

marco-ops: long term ops item: add a per-tenant SLI for successful requests (no 429/503) and expose a usage forecast on the Console so customers can preview burst headroom. Filing infra ticket INF-492: "Console: burst headroom visualization + forecast".

sarah-support: assigning follow-ups: Ingrid to finalize dashboards/alerts, Marco to file infra ticket and review rate-limiter config for dynamic burst increases, Alex to add repro snippet to support KB. Jordan — flag here when you're ready to test. :thumbsup:
